subject_line: Your First Drink on Carnivore Will Surprise You
opening: This week we're talking about the thing nobody wants to admit: what actually happens when you have a drink on carnivore. Sarah's not judging, but she's not sugarcoating it either. Plus, I'm still buzzing from Meatstock 2026 (1,600 carnivores in one room is exactly as intense as it sounds), Marcus breaks down how to lose fat and build muscle at the same time, and Sarah explains why your TikTok feed won't shut up about beef tallow.

hero.title: Carnivore and Alcohol: What Happens When You Drink
hero.teaser: You used to handle two drinks just fine. Then you went carnivore, and suddenly two drinks hit like six. The hangover the next morning was something else entirely. There's a real metabolic reason this happens, and once you understand it, you'll never look at that glass of wine the same way.
hero.cta: Read before your next social event

supporting.title: Meatstock 2026: What 1,600 Carnivores in One Room Looks Like
supporting.teaser: Chloe walked the floor at Meatstock 2026 and came back with one observation that reframes everything people say about carnivore being a fringe diet.

supporting.title: Carnivore Recomp: Losing Fat and Building Muscle at the Same Time
supporting.teaser: I put together a 12-week protocol with specific daily protein targets for losing fat and building muscle on carnivore at the same time, and the data on whether it actually works might surprise you.

supporting.title: What Beef Tallow Actually Does (And Why It's Trending)
supporting.teaser: Your grandmother cooked with beef tallow every single day, then an entire generation was told to throw it out. So why are top chefs and nutrition researchers quietly bringing it back?

try_this_week: Cook one meal this week in beef tallow instead of your usual oil. Sear a steak or roast some vegetables and watch the browning. Tallow gives you a deeper crust, richer flavor, and meals that actually keep you full through the afternoon. It's a simple swap you can taste immediately.
looking_ahead: I've been running the same lifting program for three months but shifting when I eat my biggest meal relative to training, and the recovery numbers went somewhere I didn't expect.
